_meta.description: oh-my-mlip public MLIP registry. Agents and users read this to resolve each model's environment, interpreter, and inference code.
_meta.source_policy: Each framework's env+model is unified to the fastest validated setup. Same checkpoint = same accuracy; only speed differs across contributors.

field_guide.env: conda env name; install.sh builds it from envs/<env>.yml into ${OH_MY_MLIP_HOME}/envs/<env>
field_guide.default_version: optional; for a multi-version framework, the version key resolve() selects when version=None. Must be one of the framework's version keys.
field_guide.python: interpreter path of that framework's env, ${OH_MY_MLIP_HOME}-relative (do NOT use conda activate)
field_guide.import: import lines for the top of a generated run script
field_guide.arch_pinned: if true, pick the inference_<arch> variant matching the host GPU (sm86=A5000/A6000, sm89=L40S, ...; auto-detected via registry.detect_host_arch). A generic 'inference' block may carry the ${OMM_ARCH} placeholder, which resolve() expands to the arch in use — so ANY host arch resolves and the per-arch .pt2 is compiled on the user GPU on first run, never distributed
field_guide.status: free-form provenance/validation provenance string carried verbatim from the internal registry
field_guide.env_run: optional env-var prefix that MUST wrap the interpreter invocation (key=value allowlist only; e.g. LD_LIBRARY_PATH="")
field_guide.gated: bool. if true, weights require accepting an upstream license and using the user's own HF_TOKEN; gated weights are NEVER redistributed by this repo
field_guide.license_url: string|null. URL of the upstream weights license to accept before download (set for gated models)
field_guide.weights: how weights are obtained: 'bundled' (inside the framework's own pip package) | 'auto-download' (fetched by name to a shared cache on first run) | 'on-demand-hf' (fetched from Hugging Face Hub, may be gated)
field_guide.weights_fetch: fetch mechanism: 'by-name' (resolved by model name/cache) | 'url' (explicit download URL) | 'gated-hf' (gated HF repo requiring license acceptance + HF_TOKEN)
field_guide.weights_source: the source value matching weights_fetch: an HF repo id (owner/name) for gated-hf, an http(s) URL (or the 'TODO-owner-review' placeholder while no official link is recorded) for url, a resolver name/placeholder for by-name
field_guide.weights_fetch_command: optional argv template for by-name weights that still need an explicit local models/<env>/ path; {weights_source} and {target_root} are available
field_guide.weights_cache_env: optional env var set to the target root before running weights_fetch_command
field_guide.validation: GPU validation state across two independent axes: ARCH-VALIDITY: 'validated_sm86' or 'validated_sm89' indicates the compiled artifact is valid for that compute capability and transfers across same-architecture hosts. HOST-RESOURCE/DRIVER-VALIDITY: a separate concern (VRAM ceiling, CUDA driver compatibility) that does not transfer and must be verified on each host. A validated_sm89 label is an architecture claim only; on different sm89 hardware it may still require fallback to CPU due to host-specific resource or driver constraints. Other states: 'gpu_pending' (environment loads but GPU computation not yet verified) or 'cpu_only'. The source of truth for any given host is measured local results, not carried labels.

_meta.catbench: All environments include catbench. D3 dispersion correction: from catbench.dispersion import DispersionCorrection; calc = DispersionCorrection().apply(calc). The architecture-specific pair_d3.so is recompiled on the user's GPU on first run; requires nvcc (see env.sh).
_meta.note: All models are at their actual validation state. Rows marked validation='gpu_pending' have loaded successfully but GPU computation is not yet verified.

NequIP.note: Architecture-pinned: auto-detects host GPU (sm86 vs sm89) and selects the compiled artifact. NequIPCalculator requires from_compiled_model() with a pre-compiled .pt2 file; this is recompiled on the user's GPU on first run and cached locally. Runtime requires ninja on PATH and nvrtc.h accessible (set by env.sh); compilation happens once on a cold cache and loads from ~/.cache/torch_extensions on subsequent runs.

accel.load_note: import openequivariance; NequIPCalculator.from_compiled_model(<file>, device='cuda')  (use a torchscript .nequip.pth for torch<2.10; LAMMPS deploy: nequip-prepare-lmp-mliap)

NequIP-OAM-XL.note: GPU-validated on sm89. Requires compilation of arch-specific .pt2 artifact. The openequivariance backend uses JIT compilation on first load with MAX_JOBS=4 to avoid hangs on systems with process limits; subsequent runs load from cache at ~/.cache/torch_extensions.

finetune.semantics: finetune: model._target_: ModelFromPackage/ModelFromCheckpoint loads weights only into a fresh run. nequip-train ++ckpt_path=<ckpt> is the separate resume mechanism restoring optimizer/scheduler state.

Allegro.note: Architecture-pinned. Uses cuEquivariance (cueq) backend, not openequivariance. The cueq ops ship as pre-built wheels (cuequivariance-ops-cu12), so no runtime JIT compilation is needed. NequIPCalculator requires from_compiled_model() with a pre-compiled .pt2 file; the architecture-specific artifact is recompiled on the user's GPU on first run and cached locally.

accel.install: cuequivariance + cuequivariance-torch + cuequivariance-ops-cu12/-torch-cu12 are pinned in envs/allegro.yml (no separate install); they provide the tensor_product op schemas the AOT .pt2 needs at load.
accel.load_note: import cuequivariance_torch; NequIPCalculator.from_compiled_model(<file>, device='cuda')  (use a torchscript .nequip.pth for torch<2.10; do NOT add --modifiers enable_OpenEquivariance — that is NequIP-only)

Nequix.note: Nequix uses the JAX backend with native .nqx checkpoint format. Pass backend='jax' and use_kernel=False for e3nn-jax tensor products (no OpenEquivariance build required). Weights files must retain the .nqx extension; renaming to .pt triggers unnecessary torch-JAX conversion attempts.

finetune.semantics: finetune_from loads weights only (atom_energies/scale/shift may also be overridden on the torch backend). resume_from is the separate mechanism restoring full training state.

DeePMD.note: Must run with LD_LIBRARY_PATH='' to avoid conflicts with system Intel oneAPI libfabric that clash with deepmd's mpich dependency.

DPA-3.1-3M-FT.note: Weights are downloaded and frozen from a multi-task checkpoint to a single-head frozen model by prepare_deepmd_weights.py (run automatically during install). finetune.semantics: finetune: --finetune <ckpt> loads weights (fitting net re-initialized unless --use-pretrain-script or a matching model section is given). --model-branch selects which head to start from for a multi-task checkpoint. The shipped checkpoint (dpa-3.1-3m-ft.pth) is itself a multi-task fine-tuned model (31 heads), so --model-branch here selects among existing heads rather than adapting a base-only checkpoint.
finetune.note: dpdata==1.1.0 is pinned in the environment and required for dataset processing.
finetune.reason: the shipped variant is itself already a fine-tune (a 31-head multi-task checkpoint derived from the base DPA-3.1-3M model), so --model-branch semantics here (choosing among existing downstream heads) differ from fine-tuning a base-only foundation checkpoint

ORB.note: Conservative inference mode with float32-high precision. Uses CPU for neighbor list construction; performance depends on host CPU load.
